column1: # Grammar patterns and everyday expressions Wiktionary lacks as entries. word<TAB>gloss

column2: to have just — Acabo de comer = I just ate
to be going to — Voy a salir = I'm going to go out
to have to, must — Tengo que irme = I have to go
to be supposed to, must — He de decirte algo = I must tell you something
must be, probably — Debe de estar en casa = He/she must be home
to do again — Volvió a llamar = He called again
to keep on, still be doing — Sigo trabajando = I'm still working
to be (doing) right now — Estoy comiendo = I'm eating
to have been doing — Llevo dos años aquí = I've been here two years
to start (doing) suddenly — Se puso a llorar = She started crying
to begin to — Empezó a llover = It began to rain
to begin to — Comenzó a cantar = He began to sing
to stop, quit — Dejé de fumar = I quit smoking
to finish — Terminé de leer = I finished reading
to burst out — Se echó a reír = He burst out laughing
to usually — Suelo levantarme temprano = I usually get up early
to try to — Trato de dormir = I'm trying to sleep
to take (time) to — Tardó en responder = It took him a while to answer
to mean — ¿Qué quiere decir? = What does it mean?
to not matter — Me da igual = I don't care, it's all the same
one must, it is necessary to — Hay que ir = We have to go
almost — Ya casi llego = I'm almost there
just in case
maybe, perhaps
suddenly
from time to time
at least
however, nevertheless
as soon as
more and more
to realize — Me di cuenta = I realized
to miss — Te extraño/Te echo de menos = I miss you
to feel like — Tengo ganas de salir = I feel like going out
to be about to; to be yet to be done — Está por llover = It's about to rain
to be going around — Anda diciendo mentiras = He's going around telling lies
